question.:question/problem: Given that $f(x)=-10{e}^{x}+2$, the slope of the tangent line at $x=ln⁡9$ is{{field-1}}.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The derivative of ${e}^{x}$ is just ${e}^{x}$ itself. On the other hand, $2$ is a constant, so its derivative is $0.$

First, using the addition rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-10{e}^{x}+2) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-10{e}^{x})+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2) \\  & =-10\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({e}^{x})+0 \\  & =-10{e}^{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent at $x=ln⁡9$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=ln⁡9} & ={(-10{e}^{x})\,|}_{x=ln⁡9} \\  & =-10{e}^{ln⁡9} \\  & =-10\cdot 9 \\  & =-90.\end{aligned}
$$
